title.zh: DNS、邮件和视频通话：三道简答题（第 15、13、14 题）

description.en: The services DNS provides besides name lookup, why email needed MIME and how MIME works within SMTP, and why the buffer that smooths a stream is a problem in a conversation.
description.zh: DNS 除了查名字还提供哪些服务，邮件为什么需要 MIME、MIME 怎样在 SMTP 之内工作，以及让流媒体平稳的缓冲为什么在对话里成了问题。

name.en: What DNS is for: translating domain names to IP addresses (name resolution)
name.zh: DNS 的作用：把域名翻译成 IP 地址 (name resolution)

name.en: Other DNS services: host aliasing, mail server registry, load distribution
name.zh: DNS 的其他服务：别名、邮件服务器登记、负载分担 (host aliasing, mail server registry, load distribution)

title.zh: 第 15 题原文
模拟卷 · 第 15 题（2 分）

paras.en: Briefly describe two services that DNS provides using bullet points.
paras.zh: 用要点简要描述 DNS 提供的两项服务。

items.en: **DNS**, the Domain Name System, is the Internet's directory of names: a distributed database run by many name servers.
items.zh: **DNS**（域名系统）是互联网的名字目录：由许多域名服务器共同维护的一个分布式数据库。

items.en: **Two services**, 2 marks: two bullets, each naming a service and saying in a sentence what it does. The obvious one counts, and one more is needed.
items.zh: **两项服务**，2 分：两条要点，每条说出一项服务，再用一句话说它做什么。最常见的那项算一项，还得再写一项。

chapter.zh: 第 15 题：DNS 提供什么

title.zh: DNS 做什么

text.en: Its main job is **name resolution**. People remember names such as www.unimelb.edu.au; packets need IP addresses. DNS translates the name into the address, and only then can anything be sent. The course names three more services, each a different kind of record in the same database:
text.zh: 它的主要任务是**域名解析**。人记得住 www.unimelb.edu.au 这样的名字；分组要的是 IP 地址。DNS 把名字翻译成地址，然后才能发东西。课上还讲了另外三项服务，每项对应同一个数据库里的一种记录：

items.en: **Host aliasing**: an easy name can be an alias for the real, **canonical** name of a host. The course's example: www.unimelb.edu.au is an alias of squizedge-cloud.cms.unimelb.edu.au.
items.zh: **主机别名**：一个好记的名字可以是主机真正的**规范名**（canonical name）的别名。课上的例子：www.unimelb.edu.au 是 squizedge-cloud.cms.unimelb.edu.au 的别名。

items.en: **Mail server registry**: DNS says which server accepts mail for a domain. A message to someone@unimelb.edu.au first asks DNS for unimelb.edu.au's mail server.
items.zh: **邮件服务器登记**：DNS 告诉你哪台服务器接收某个域的邮件。发往 someone@unimelb.edu.au 的信，先要问 DNS：unimelb.edu.au 的邮件服务器是哪台。

items.en: **Load distribution and redundancy**: a large site runs several servers, each with its own address, and DNS associates all of them with one canonical name. It rotates the order of the addresses in its replies, so different clients start with different servers; if one server is down, a client can try the next address.
items.zh: **负载分配和冗余**：大网站跑着好几台服务器，各有各的地址，DNS 把它们都关联到同一个规范名上。它在每次回答时轮换地址的顺序，于是不同的客户端从不同的服务器开始；某台服务器坏了，客户端可以试下一个地址。

alt.en: A name server answers three clients for www.shop.com with the same three addresses in rotated order: .1 .2 .3, then .2 .3 .1, then .3 .1 .2. Each client connects to the first address it was given, so the three clients reach three different servers.
alt.zh: 一台域名服务器为 www.shop.com 回答三个客户端，给的是同样三个地址，但顺序轮换：.1 .2 .3、.2 .3 .1、.3 .1 .2。每个客户端连接拿到的第一个地址，于是三个客户端分到了三台不同的服务器。

caption.en: Load distribution: the same three addresses, a different one first each time. Each client takes the first, and the load spreads over the servers.
caption.zh: 负载分配：同样三个地址，每次排第一的不一样。每个客户端取第一个，负载就分摊到了各台服务器上。

title.zh: 第 15 题：满分答案

text.en: Two bullets: name resolution, and one of the other three. Each says what DNS does and what for.
text.zh: 两条：域名解析，再加另外三项中的一项。每条都说 DNS 做什么、为了什么。

title.en: Practice exam, Q15 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 15 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Name resolution: DNS translates a host name (e.g. www.unimelb.edu.au) into its IP address, which is needed to send packets to that host.
paras.zh: 域名解析：DNS 把主机名（例如 www.unimelb.edu.au）翻译成它的 IP 地址，向该主机发送分组需要这个地址。

paras.en: Load distribution: a set of IP addresses of replicated servers is associated with one canonical name, and the DNS server rotates the order of the addresses in its replies, so the clients' requests are spread over the servers (and if one server is down, a client can try another).
paras.zh: 负载分配：把一组副本服务器的 IP 地址关联到同一个规范名上，DNS 服务器在回答中轮换这些地址的顺序，使客户端的请求分散到各台服务器（某台服务器宕机时，客户端还可以试另一台）。

text.en: Also accepted as the second bullet: **host aliasing** (an alias name mapped to the host's canonical name) or the **mail server registry** (finding the server that accepts mail for a domain).
text.zh: 第二条也可以写：**主机别名**（把别名映射到主机的规范名），或**邮件服务器登记**（找出接收某个域邮件的服务器）。

title.zh: 第 13 题原文
模拟卷 · 第 13 题（3 分）

paras.en: Why was MIME introduced as an extension to SMTP, and what limitations did it address?
paras.zh: 为什么要引入 MIME 作为 SMTP 的扩展？它解决了哪些局限？

items.en: **SMTP** moves mail from the sender's user agent to its mail server and on to the recipient's mail server. It carries a message made of headers and a body.
items.zh: **SMTP** 把邮件从发件人的用户代理送到它的邮件服务器，再送到收件人的邮件服务器。它运的是一封由头部和正文组成的信。

items.en: **MIME**, Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions. *An extension*: it adds to email rather than replacing anything.
items.zh: **MIME**，多用途互联网邮件扩展。*扩展*：它是给邮件加东西，不是替换掉什么。

items.en: **What limitations**: what email could not carry before MIME. 3 marks: the limitation, what MIME adds, what that makes possible.
items.zh: **解决了哪些局限**：有 MIME 之前邮件运不了什么。3 分：局限是什么、MIME 加了什么、因此能做什么。

chapter.zh: 第 13 题：为什么要 MIME

title.zh: 有 MIME 之前和之后的邮件

text.en: In the early days of email, messages were in English and used only ASCII, and the message format (RFC 822) and SMTP reflected that: a message is lines of **7-bit ASCII** text. In time the limits became clear. The course lists four: languages with accents (French, Spanish); non-Latin alphabets (Cyrillic); languages without an alphabet (Chinese, Japanese); and content that is not text at all (audio, images).
text.zh: 电子邮件早期，信都是英文，只用 ASCII，消息格式（RFC 822）和 SMTP 也是照这个设计的：一封信就是若干行 **7 位 ASCII** 文本。后来局限就显出来了。课上列了四种：带重音的语言（法语、西班牙语）；非拉丁字母（西里尔字母）；不用字母的语言（中文、日文）；以及根本不是文本的内容（音频、图片）。

text.en: MIME's answer is to leave SMTP alone and add **structure and encoding rules** to the message itself. Five new headers say what the body is and how it was wrapped; the two that matter most are **Content-Type** (text/plain, text/html, image/jpeg, video/mp4, ...) and **Content-Transfer-Encoding** (how non-ASCII data is turned into ASCII for the trip). **Base64** turns every 3 bytes into 4 ASCII characters, so any data can travel, at 4/3 of its size. A **multipart** body holds several independent parts, such as text and an attachment, separated by a boundary line.
text.zh: MIME 的办法是不动 SMTP，而是给信本身加上**结构和编码规则**。五个新的头部说明正文是什么、是怎么包装的；最要紧的两个是 **Content-Type**（text/plain、text/html、image/jpeg、video/mp4……）和 **Content-Transfer-Encoding**（为了运送，怎样把非 ASCII 数据变成 ASCII）。**Base64** 把每 3 个字节变成 4 个 ASCII 字符，什么数据都能运，代价是体积变成 4/3。**多部分**（multipart）正文可以装好几个独立的部分，比如正文加一个附件，用一条分隔线隔开。

blocks.code:
From: alice@unimelb.edu.au
To: bob@example.com
Subject: Photo
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary="xyz"

--xyz
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8

你好 Bob, the photo is attached.
--xyz
Content-Type: image/jpeg
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64

/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABAQEASABIAAD/2wBDAAMCAgMCAgMDAwMEAwMEBQgFBQQE...
--xyz--

caption.en: A multipart message: a text part in UTF-8 and a JPEG photo in base64, separated by the boundary --xyz.
caption.zh: 一封多部分的信：一部分是 UTF-8 文本，一部分是 base64 编码的 JPEG 照片，用分隔线 --xyz 隔开。

text.en: On the wire, all of it is still 7-bit ASCII lines, so every SMTP server in the world carries a MIME message without knowing anything about MIME. Only the user agents at the two ends need to understand it.
text.zh: 在线路上，这一切仍然是一行行 7 位 ASCII 文本，所以全世界的 SMTP 服务器都能照常运送 MIME 邮件，完全不用懂 MIME。只有两端的用户代理需要理解它。

prompt.en: Why is the photo sent in base64 rather than as its raw bytes?
prompt.zh: 照片为什么要用 base64 发，而不是直接发原始字节？

feedback.en: Base64 makes data a third larger.
feedback.zh: Base64 会让数据大三分之一。

label.en: SMTP carries 7-bit ASCII text; raw bytes could be misread or damaged on the way
label.zh: SMTP 运的是 7 位 ASCII 文本；原始字节在路上可能被误读或损坏

label.en: Because MIME replaced SMTP with a binary protocol
label.zh: 因为 MIME 用二进制协议取代了 SMTP

feedback.en: MIME changed the message, not the protocol: SMTP still carries text.
feedback.zh: MIME 改的是信，不是协议：SMTP 运的仍然是文本。

explain.en: Base64 wraps any bytes as plain ASCII characters, which SMTP carries safely; the receiving user agent unwraps them.
explain.zh: Base64 把任意字节包装成普通的 ASCII 字符，SMTP 能安全运送；收件方的用户代理再拆开。

title.zh: 第 13 题：满分答案

text.en: Three links: the limitation (7-bit ASCII, so plain English text only); what MIME adds (content types, encodings such as base64, multipart); what became possible (other languages, non-text content).
text.zh: 三环：局限（7 位 ASCII，所以只能是英文纯文本）；MIME 加了什么（内容类型、base64 之类的编码、多部分）；因此能做什么（别的语言、非文本内容）。

title.en: Practice exam, Q13 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 13 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: SMTP and the original message format (RFC 822) only supported 7-bit ASCII text, which limited email to plain English text. MIME was introduced to extend the message format without changing SMTP: it adds headers that give the content type (e.g. text/html, image/jpeg) and a transfer encoding (e.g. base64) that wraps any data as ASCII, and it allows multipart messages. This lets email carry languages with accents and non-Latin or non-alphabetic scripts (e.g. Chinese, in UTF-8), and non-text content such as images, audio, video and attachments.
paras.zh: SMTP 和最初的消息格式（RFC 822）只支持 7 位 ASCII 文本，邮件因此只能是英文纯文本。引入 MIME 是为了在不改变 SMTP 的前提下扩展消息格式：它加入了说明内容类型的头部（例如 text/html、image/jpeg）和把任意数据包装成 ASCII 的传输编码（例如 base64），并支持多部分的邮件。这样邮件就能承载带重音的语言、非拉丁或非字母文字（例如 UTF-8 编码的中文），以及图片、音频、视频和附件等非文本内容。

title.zh: 第 14 题原文
模拟卷 · 第 14 题（2 分）

paras.en: A common approach to removing jitter in streaming audio is to buffer incoming packets at the receiver. Briefly explain a key problem using this approach for video conferencing.
paras.zh: 消除流式音频中抖动的一种常见做法，是在接收方缓冲到达的分组。简要说明把这种做法用于视频会议时的一个关键问题。

items.en: **Jitter**: the variation in delay from one packet to the next. Packets sent at an even pace arrive unevenly.
items.zh: **抖动**（jitter）：分组与分组之间延迟的变化。匀速发出的分组，到达时却快慢不一。

items.en: **Buffer incoming packets at the receiver**: hold them for a while before playing them, then play at an even pace.
items.zh: **在接收方缓冲到达的分组**：先攒一会儿再播，然后匀速地播。

items.en: **Video conferencing** against **streaming audio**: a conversation in both directions, live, against listening to a stream. 2 marks: the property of conferencing, and the problem it causes.
items.zh: **视频会议**对比**流式音频**：双向的、实时的对话，对比单向地听一个流。2 分：视频会议的特点，以及它带来的问题。

alt.en: Six packets sent at an even pace arrive with uneven delays; the fourth arrives very late. With a large buffer, playback starts after 140 and every packet is in time. With a small buffer, playback starts after 80; the fourth packet arrives after its turn and is skipped.
alt.zh: 六个分组匀速发出，到达时延迟不一；第四个到得很晚。用大缓冲时，播放在 140 之后开始，每个分组都赶得上。用小缓冲时，播放在 80 之后开始；第四个分组过了它的播放时刻才到，被跳过。

caption.en: A buffer hides jitter by waiting. The large buffer plays every packet, but starts late; the small one starts soon and loses the packet that came too late.
caption.zh: 缓冲靠“等”来掩盖抖动。大缓冲每个分组都播到了，但开始得晚；小缓冲开始得早，却丢掉了那个迟到太久的分组。

text.en: The buffer removes jitter by **adding delay**: every packet is played the length of the buffer after it was sent, early ones wait longer and late ones less. The course's trade-off: a small buffer starts playing quickly but is susceptible to jitter; a large buffer has a delay at the start but is less susceptible.
text.zh: 缓冲消除抖动的办法是**加延迟**：每个分组都在发出后、隔着缓冲那么长的时间才播放，早到的多等，晚到的少等。课上讲的取舍：小缓冲开播快，但容易受抖动影响；大缓冲开头有延迟，但不怕抖动。

text.en: For streaming audio, a few seconds of waiting at the start costs nothing: the stream goes one way, and nobody is waiting to reply. A video conference is **two-way and interactive**: every second of buffer is a second before the other side hears you, and a second more before you hear their answer. Replies come late, people interrupt and talk over each other, the conversation stops feeling live. (For telephony, the ITU's guideline G.114 recommends keeping one-way delay below about 150 ms.) So the course's advice for real-time conferencing: keep the buffer **small**, **skip** packets that arrive too late, adjust the video quality, and use the network's quality-of-service support where it exists.
text.zh: 对流式音频来说，开头等几秒没什么损失：流是单向的，没人等着回话。视频会议是**双向、交互**的：缓冲多一秒，对方就晚一秒听到你，你也再晚一秒听到对方的回答。回应总是慢半拍，大家互相打断、抢着说话，对话就不像在面对面了。（国际电信联盟 ITU 的 G.114 建议，通话的单向延迟最好不超过约 150 ms。）所以课上对实时会议的建议是：缓冲要**小**，迟到太久的分组直接**跳过**，调整视频质量，网络能提供服务质量保障时就用上。

title.zh: 第 14 题：满分答案

text.en: Two links: conferencing is two-way and interactive; buffering adds delay, which harms interaction. A third line on what conferencing does instead shows you understand the trade-off.
text.zh: 两环：视频会议是双向、交互的；缓冲会增加延迟，而延迟伤害交互。再加一句会议实际怎么做，能看出你懂这个取舍。

title.en: Practice exam, Q14 · a full-mark answer
title.zh: 模拟卷第 14 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Video conferencing is a two-way, interactive service. Buffering removes jitter only by delaying playback: every packet waits in the buffer, so the buffer's length is added to the end-to-end delay. A large buffer makes the conversation lag (people wait for replies and talk over each other), so conferencing must keep the buffer small and skip packets that arrive too late, accepting some glitches.
paras.zh: 视频会议是双向的交互式服务。缓冲消除抖动的代价是推迟播放：每个分组都要在缓冲区里等，缓冲的长度就加到了端到端延迟上。缓冲大了，对话就会滞后（等回应、互相抢话），所以视频会议只能用小缓冲，并跳过迟到太久的分组，接受一些卡顿。

title.zh: 三种流媒体

rows.zh: 重传（用 TCP 没问题）

rows.en: no time to retransmit: FEC, concealment
rows.zh: 来不及重传：前向纠错、错误掩盖

rows.en: RTP over UDP; SIP to set up the call
rows.zh: RTP 跑在 UDP 上；用 SIP 建立通话

text.en: Read the table by the first row. Who is waiting for whom decides how much delay is tolerable, and that decides the buffer, how losses are handled and the transport.
text.zh: 按第一行来读这张表。谁在等谁，决定了能忍受多少延迟，进而决定了缓冲多大、丢包怎么处理、用什么传输协议。

title.en: Your turn: three servers, one name
title.zh: 你来：三台服务器，一个名字

prompt.en: A shop's website runs on three servers with different IP addresses. Which DNS service spreads the visitors over them?
prompt.zh: 一家网店的网站跑在三台 IP 地址不同的服务器上。哪项 DNS 服务能把访客分摊到它们上面？

label.en: Load distribution: one name, all three addresses, in a rotating order
label.zh: 负载分配：一个名字对应三个地址，顺序轮换

feedback.en: Aliasing maps another name to the canonical name; it does not choose between servers.
feedback.zh: 别名是把另一个名字映射到规范名；它不负责在服务器之间挑选。

feedback.en: That finds the server that accepts a domain's mail.
feedback.zh: 那是找接收某个域邮件的服务器。

explain.en: DNS rotates the order of the addresses in its replies; each client starts with the first, so the load spreads.
explain.zh: DNS 在回答里轮换地址的顺序；每个客户端从第一个开始，负载就分开了。

title.zh: 你来：哪个需要 MIME

prompt.en: Which of these could email not carry before MIME?
prompt.zh: 有 MIME 之前，下面哪个邮件运不了？

feedback.en: That is exactly what 7-bit ASCII was designed for.
feedback.zh: 7 位 ASCII 正是为它设计的。

explain.en: Chinese characters are not in 7-bit ASCII; MIME lets the body declare a character set such as UTF-8 and encode it for the trip.
explain.zh: 汉字不在 7 位 ASCII 里；MIME 让正文声明字符集（比如 UTF-8），再为运送做编码。

title.en: Your turn: a live match and a phone call
title.zh: 你来：直播比赛和打电话

prompt.en: A live sports stream can buffer 10 seconds, but an Internet phone call cannot. Briefly explain why.
prompt.zh: 一场体育直播可以缓冲 10 秒，网络电话却不行。简要解释为什么。

key_points.en: The sports stream is one-way: nobody replies, so a fixed delay is not noticed
key_points.zh: 体育直播是单向的：没人回话，固定的延迟察觉不到

key_points.en: A call is two-way and interactive: the buffer adds to the delay of every exchange
key_points.zh: 通话是双向交互的：缓冲会加到每一次一来一回的延迟上

key_points.en: So a call keeps a small buffer and skips late packets
key_points.zh: 所以通话用小缓冲，迟到的分组直接跳过

model_answer.en: The sports stream goes one way, so a 10-second delay just means the viewer sees everything 10 seconds late, which nobody notices. A call is two-way and interactive: the buffer is added to every exchange, and 10 seconds would make conversation impossible. So a call keeps its buffer small and skips packets that arrive too late.
model_answer.zh: 体育直播是单向的，延迟 10 秒只是观众晚 10 秒看到一切，没人会察觉。通话是双向交互的：缓冲会加到每一次一来一回上，10 秒根本没法对话。所以通话用小缓冲，迟到太久的分组直接跳过。

explain.en: The same buffer trade-off, decided by whether anyone is waiting to reply.
explain.zh: 同一个缓冲取舍，由有没有人等着回话来决定。
